summary: The task's core factual claim checks out on live verification -- PR #492 (commits 3dfc0aa1/b4220392) is already an ancestor of HEAD, erp-einvoice-service.ts/einvoice-format.ts have no hardcoded GstRt:0, and einvoice-format.test.ts asserts GstRt is 18 on the IN path -- so declaring V2-21's code half already shipped and making no source change was the right call, and the pre-existing ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml YAML parse error at lines 43/276 was independently confirmed to already exist on the parent commit (unrelated to this diff, not introduced or worsened by it). However, the diff's own stated deliverable in ai-os/boss/ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml -- 'moved the V2-1 claim ... from active: to here' -- did not actually happen: the original V2-1/UAE-country-pack entry (session_label containing 'task-20260720-022700-superboss-v2-plan') is still present verbatim under the active: block (starting line 2943, before the recently_completed: key at line 3049), with only a trailing sentence edited out of its text. A new summary entry was added under recently_completed: (~line 3078) claiming the move happened and explicitly asserting 'this entry had sat unmoved in active: for 6 days past merge' -- but it remains unmoved even after this task, now duplicated in both sections. Since ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml's entire purpose (per Rule 11 / the file's own header) is to let other sessions trust active: as real in-flight work and avoid duplicate-work collisions, a false 'already moved to recently_completed' claim sitting next to the still-active stale entry is a real correctness defect in the exact registry other sessions rely on, not a cosmetic nit -- it should be fixed (actually delete the stale entry from active:) before merge.
issues: ai-os/boss/ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml: the pre-existing V2-1/UAE-country-pack entry (session_label 'task-20260720-022700-superboss-v2-plan...') is still present under active: (line ~2943), not removed as the new recently_completed: entry (~line 3078) and PROGRESS.md both claim ('moved the V2-1 claim ... from active: to here'). The entry now exists in both active: and recently_completed:, contradicting the diff's own narrative and leaving a 6-day-stale claim visible to other sessions as if still in-flight.
